newsitem.title: USA: Russian banks lack strong government support - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Russian banks lack strong government support - S&P.

text.p: Russian banks are rated at least a notch below the country's BB-minus long-term foreign currency rating because the Russian banking sector lacks strong government support, Standard & Poor's said Tuesday.
Russia's central bank does not have a "too-big-to-fail" attitude and has allowed some of the nation's largest banks to fail in the past, S&P banking analyst Tanya Azarch noted in a conference call.
"We have not factored in government support or system support for the Russian banks to any large extent," Azarch said.
"Until we see them actually move to recapitalize a bank that has failed ... we are reluctant to say there is a lot of government support for the Russian banks," she said.

S&P issued its first ratings for Russian banks in recent days. Three banks -- Alfa Bank, Rossiyskiy Kredit Bank and Aljba Alliance -- received single-B long-term counterparty ratings, while SBS-Agro garnered a B-plus.
Formerly dedicated to serving the financial needs of specific industrial groups, many Russian banks have diversified into other commercial and retail operations, Azarch said.
The retail banking sector, however, remains largely undeveloped and must be expanded in order to secure Russia's economic recovery, she said.
"The retail sector is extremely small still in Russia," Azarch said. "Nevertheless, for the Russian program to succeed, the retail sector will have to grow."
SBS-Agro holds a ratings edge over the other three S&P-rated banks largely because of its retail and commercial presence, the analyst said.
Azarch declined to comment on the creditworthiness of other Russian banks.
